about: Pit Lane: the day's top 10 Supercars stories. Headlines and summaries are written for Monaro.co.uk; links go to the original stories. Newest day first. A link with "archived" points to a saved copy; "gone": true means the source removed the story.

stories.h: Mostert and Feeney question bigger seeding gaps
stories.t: This year's seeding leaves Feeney 54 points and Mostert 72 behind Payne, so neither can lead after Friday's sprint even with a win. Mostert would prefer last year's tighter spread.

stories.h: Triple Eight blames tyre life for Sandown slump
stories.t: Mark Dutton says the car's balance wore the tyres too quickly, leaving Brown pushing too hard. The team missed a Sandown podium for the first time since 2017, and Brown can now support Feeney.

stories.h: Allen's slump keeps the teams' race alive
stories.t: Kai Allen was third in the standings after September but has not finished higher than 13th in five races since. Grove still leads Triple Eight by 148 points.

stories.h: Tickford's Nash relaxed despite another miss
stories.t: Co-owner Rod Nash called reaching the semi-finals a good effort, even though Tickford has now gone 11 seasons without a championship or Bathurst win.

stories.h: Tru-Blu Falcon returns for Adelaide demo
stories.t: Paul Morris will drive the restored DJR Falcon from the 2012 Bathurst 1000 in heritage demonstration runs at the last event on Adelaide's current layout.

stories.h: Feeney seeded third after tie-break mix-up
stories.t: Feeney and Mostert finished Sandown level on points. Official results first had Mostert ahead, but the Sandown tie-break rule favours Feeney for finishing Sunday's race in front, worth 96 seeding points to Mostert's 78.

stories.h: Tickford suspects tyre batch behind Waters slump
stories.t: Waters went from fifth in Q1 to 18th on the grid on a fresh set with no car changes. Team manager Matt Roberts says the evidence points to a bad batch of slicks.

stories.h: Randle stands firm over De Pasquale clash
stories.t: Thomas Randle kept De Pasquale behind on cold tyres after his stop, costing time in the chase for Payne. Randle says there are no blue flags in that phase and he was racing his own battle.

stories.h: Teams' title still open for Adelaide
stories.t: Grove's Penrite Racing stretched its lead over Triple Eight from 102 to 148 points, but 576 are available to teams in Adelaide. Brenton Grove says Payne's drivers' title bid comes first.

stories.h: Van Gisbergen gets new NASCAR crew chief
stories.t: Blake Harris, formerly with Alex Bowman at Hendrick, will lead Shane van Gisbergen's Trackhouse car in 2027. Stephen Doran returns to Spire Motorsports.

stories.h: Ojeda drops GT3 role to focus on Adelaide
stories.t: Scott Andrews will replace Jayden Ojeda in Tigani Motorsport's Mercedes at the Grand Final. Ojeda is now guaranteed to finish as the top rookie in the championship.

stories.h: Stanaway to stay with Blanchard for 2027 enduros
stories.t: Richie Stanaway has agreed a renewal to co-drive with James Golding again next year, although it is yet to be announced. Zak Best's status as BRT's other co-driver is unconfirmed.

stories.h: DJR says Kostecki's grid breach was not premeditated
stories.t: Team manager Tom Moore said Kostecki switched off to save a tiny amount of fuel, as many drivers do, but for longer. He accepted the breach but called the drive-through hefty.

stories.h: Supercars keeps testing brake fixes
stories.t: Several cars trialled different pad compounds at Monday's Sandown ride day, following a fully instrumented test at Queensland Raceway. Brake problems were a talking point at Ipswich, The Bend and Bathurst.

stories.h: Murray's first podium lifts PremiAir
stories.t: Cooper Murray finished third on Sunday in only his second round with PremiAir. The result moves the team past Blanchard in the pit lane order for Adelaide.

stories.h: Sandown crowd up on 2025
stories.t: Supercars reports 70,677 fans across three days, up 3.17 per cent, taking the season's total attendance past 1.42 million.

stories.h: Hughes heads to Taupō for early laps
stories.t: Erebus rookie Jarrod Hughes will race in New Zealand TA2 at Taupō on 13-15 November, learning a circuit that joins the Supercars calendar in 2027.

stories.h: Heimgartner keeps his main backer
stories.t: R&J Batteries will stay as primary sponsor of Andre Heimgartner's Brad Jones Racing Supra in 2027, extending a partnership that began in 2020.

stories.h: Payne wins as Grand Final four are set
stories.t: Matt Payne won from pole by seven tenths from Anton De Pasquale, who needed victory to go through. Payne, Kostecki, Feeney and Mostert will contest Adelaide, with Payne starting 30 points ahead of Kostecki.

stories.h: Kostecki penalised for switching engine off
stories.t: Already through to Adelaide, Brodie Kostecki took a drive-through after stewards found his engine was off as he rolled into his grid box, breaching start procedure rules.

stories.h: Brown and Waters knocked out of the title race
stories.t: Will Brown qualified 19th after a stuck downshift into Turn 1, and Cam Waters 18th. Both were eliminated along with De Pasquale.

stories.h: Le Brocq stays at Matt Stone Racing
stories.t: MSR has kept Jack Le Brocq for 2027, completing its line-up alongside Zach Bates, who signed a multi-year extension on Thursday.

stories.h: Exhaust damage blamed for Cameron fire
stories.t: Blanchard Racing says contact with Le Brocq folded the exhaust tips onto the side skirt, which caught fire. The crew rebuilt the Mustang overnight at the track.

stories.h: Logan takes Super2 lead into Adelaide
stories.t: Campbell Logan completed a perfect 300-point weekend and leads Brad Vaughan by nine points. Lochie Dalton, the leader before Sandown, finished fifth and drops to third.

stories.h: Questions over GM's performance role
stories.t: Rivals have asked whether Grant McPherson, who runs General Motors' data-sharing alliance, could be giving Chevrolet teams performance advice, given Supercars' strict limits on performance personnel.

stories.h: Kostecki wins his way into the Grand Final
stories.t: Brodie Kostecki's ninth win of the season makes him the first driver through to Adelaide. Matt Payne finished second and is 104 points clear of the cut-line, while Broc Feeney holds fourth by one point from Cam Waters.

stories.h: Triple Eight's day unravels
stories.t: Will Brown led after the stops but spun fighting Kostecki, then took a 15-second penalty for spinning Cameron Hill. Classified 20th, he is 88 points from the cut-line. Feeney finished 11th after double-stacking.

stories.h: Cameron escapes Mustang fire
stories.t: Aaron Cameron was unhurt after his Blanchard Ford caught fire, bringing a lap-13 Safety Car. His engineer suspects a power distribution module failure or fuel reaching the exhaust.

stories.h: Payne on pole as Mostert goes off
stories.t: Payne beat Cam Waters to pole in drying conditions. Reigning champion Chaz Mostert qualified third but had a big off in the Top Ten Shootout and started tenth.

stories.h: Allen and Le Brocq disqualified from practice
stories.t: Kai Allen lost his Practice 2 times for a rear tyre below minimum pressure. Jack Le Brocq was excluded from Practice 1 after the wrong drop gear ratio was found on his Camaro.

stories.h: Gray stays at Dick Johnson Racing
stories.t: DJR has confirmed 19-year-old Rylan Gray alongside Kostecki for 2027. He will need a new co-driver after Tony D'Alberto's retirement.

stories.h: Super2 title race opens up
stories.t: Series leader Lochie Dalton retired on the opening lap after contact with Nash Morris, his first DNF of the season. Campbell Logan won from pole.

stories.h: Supercars says wet tyre variation can't be fixed
stories.t: Teams blamed inconsistent wet tyres for swings at the Gold Coast. Tim Edwards said there is no solution, because wets are built over long periods and can sit unused for years.

stories.h: Payne fastest at Sandown as Mostert struggles
stories.t: Championship leader Matt Payne pipped Broc Feeney by 0.07 seconds in Practice 2. Chaz Mostert was only 20th after a shift-cut problem that his team expects to fix before qualifying.

stories.h: Ojeda surprises in opening practice
stories.t: PremiAir rookie Jayden Ojeda topped Practice 1, helped by an extra set of tyres. Jack Le Brocq missed the session after Matt Stone Racing found the wrong gear ratio fitted.

stories.h: Chevrolet teams rule out helping De Pasquale
stories.t: PremiAir and Erebus say they will race only for themselves at Sandown, after Supercars warned all teams about race manipulation in Thursday's briefing.

stories.h: Hughes set for full-time Erebus seat
stories.t: Barry Ryan says Erebus will definitely sign Jarrod Hughes for 2027 after his strong Gold Coast debut. Erebus's other seat remains one of the last open questions.

stories.h: Team bosses criticise calendar gaps
stories.t: Roland Dane and Barry Ryan welcome 14 rounds but say the long break around New Zealand hurts sponsors. Mostert admits he expected a third enduro.

stories.h: 2027 calendar confirmed: 14 rounds, no Ipswich
stories.t: Sydney opens in late February and Sandown closes the Sprint Cup on 27 to 29 August. Darwin holds its first night race, and Phillip Island takes the Semi Final before Adelaide's Grand Final.

stories.h: Alan Jones dies aged 80
stories.t: Australia's last Formula 1 world champion, who won the 1980 title with Williams, has died. He also started the Bathurst 1000 19 times, finishing second in 1995 and third in 1988.

stories.h: Bates signs multi-year deal with Matt Stone Racing
stories.t: Bathurst pole-sitter Zach Bates and sponsor Bendix are both committed to MSR until at least 2028, ending speculation over the rookie's future.

stories.h: Feeney and Brown to share a Mustang at the 12 Hour
stories.t: Triple Eight will run a Ford Mustang GT3 at February's Bathurst 12 Hour with its two Supercars drivers, plus a third driver likely from Ford's factory pool.

stories.h: Super2 expands to seven rounds with Mallala return
stories.t: A standalone round at Mallala in April, the series' first standalone event since 2008, means five Super2 rounds come before Bathurst next year.

stories.h: New calendar opens NASCAR door for Feeney
stories.t: San Diego and COTA no longer clash with Supercars rounds in 2027. Broc Feeney says San Diego is the race he most wants, though funding remains the hurdle.

stories.h: Reynolds accepts rear-gunner role at Sandown
stories.t: Despite his Gold Coast podium, David Reynolds says his job this weekend is to help Anton De Pasquale, who must win a race or close a 30-point gap to reach Adelaide.

stories.h: Randle's FPR throwback livery revealed
stories.t: Thomas Randle's Mustang will carry the 2007 Ford Performance Racing Bathurst colours at Sandown, unveiled with original drivers Mark Winterbottom and Steven Richards.

stories.h: Enduro Cup expansion dropped from 2027 calendar
stories.t: The 14-round calendar, due on Thursday, keeps nine Sprint Cup rounds, two enduros and three Finals rounds. Teams pushed back on co-driver costs, so a late-August Sandown will decide the Sprint Cup instead.

stories.h: Quinn hits out as Queensland Raceway is axed
stories.t: Owner Tony Quinn says fans are the main victims of Ipswich missing the 2027 calendar despite strong crowds. He says he was told only a day before the announcement and questions whether RACE are the right owners.

stories.h: Fraser lands shock Super2 drive at Sandown
stories.t: Declan Fraser will race a Matt Stone Racing Commodore in Super2 this weekend after Tommy Smith switched to a Ford. It adds to his Mustang Cup outing last weekend.

stories.h: First look at the Perth Park street circuit
stories.t: A simulation shows the 3km, 12-turn layout between Optus Stadium and Crown Casino that is expected to open the 2028 season, with a 240km/h top speed and three clear overtaking spots.

stories.h: NASCAR's Jesse Love returns for Adelaide Super2
stories.t: Last year's Xfinity champion will race Image Racing's Super2 entry at the Grand Final before moving to Ford's Wood Brothers Racing in the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027.

stories.h: 2027 grid almost settled
stories.t: Five teams, including Penrite, Red Bull Ampol and Tickford, keep the same pairings for a third year. David Reynolds remains the biggest name without a 2027 deal.

stories.h: Triple Eight teen Wickham steps up to Trans Am
stories.t: Oli Wickham, 17, makes his Trans Am debut on the Sandown 500 support bill as Triple Eight moves him towards Super2 and Supercars.

stories.h: Randle's Sandown retro honours a lost car
stories.t: Thomas Randle will run Steven Richards' 2007 Ford Performance Racing colours this weekend. The original chassis was wrecked at Eastern Creek in 2008 and scrapped a decade later.

stories.h: Feeney's 2023 Camaro returns to Bathurst
stories.t: The Red Bull Camaro that won the 2023 Sandown 500 will run at Challenge Bathurst this month in the hands of collector Mark Tracey. It is the first Gen3 car at the event.

stories.h: D'Alberto retires from Supercars co-driving
stories.t: Tony D'Alberto says this year's Bathurst, his 22nd start and 11th with DJR, was his last. He stays on as a team ambassador, and DJR says it has a shortlist for his replacement.

stories.h: Lia Block heads to the Adelaide Grand Final
stories.t: Ken Block's daughter, a recent F1 Academy race winner, will drive a Skoda Fabia in the rally festival alongside the Supercars decider on 26 to 29 November.

stories.h: Mustang Cup champion wins Triple Eight test
stories.t: Josh Anderson took the first Mustang Cup title by 62 points at Sandown, earning a run in a Red Bull Ampol Supercar at a date still to be confirmed.

stories.h: Is technical parity on the brink?
stories.t: V8 Sleuth argues last week's Super2 Commodore change, made to cars unchanged since 2020, suggests Supercars is moving from technical parity towards balancing performance by results.

stories.h: Tickford still hunting for speed before Sandown
stories.t: Cam Waters goes to Sandown as sixth seed but has no top-six finish in his last seven races. Rod Nash admits the team has not found the speed it has been missing all season.

stories.h: Feeney sees no clear title favourite
stories.t: Second seed Broc Feeney, 30 points behind Matt Payne, says any of the seven semi-finalists could be champion, and that Sandown will be tough to get through.

stories.h: Erebus explains its Gold Coast fuel error
stories.t: Barry Ryan says a young data engineer marked the fuel tower at 70 litres instead of 80, forcing Jarrod Hughes' late stop. He rejected cheating claims and called it an honest mistake.

stories.h: GM plans a two-way street with NASCAR
stories.t: GM's Simon McNamara says it wants to be Supercars' strongest manufacturer by sending young drivers and engineers to the US and bringing international GM talent to Australia. Anton De Pasquale was evaluated earlier this year.

stories.h: How the 2027 calendar is shaping up
stories.t: Speedcafe expects Sydney to open in late February, Queensland Raceway to drop off, Sandown to move to late August and Phillip Island to host a Finals round. Bathurst is set for 10 October.

stories.h: Late Super2 parity change angers Tickford
stories.t: Supercars has tweaked the Holden Commodore's boot lid gurney before Sandown, the first change to the Gen2 cars since 2022. Tickford says it was told, not consulted, and called the decision bizarre.

stories.h: Feeney wants no part in Ford team games
stories.t: Asked whether he would help another Ford team through, Broc Feeney said he is only focused on winning races, after Kostecki's teammate Rylan Gray briefly held him up on the Gold Coast.

stories.h: Perkins: Camaro teams copied each other's fuel maths
stories.t: Jack Perkins says pit stop times back the denials of any GM plot, and believes PremiAir short-fuelled Murray after following Erebus' mistaken stop for Hughes a lap earlier.

stories.h: Bendix says new owners are lined up
stories.t: Matt Stone Racing's sponsor says the ownership change will separate its parent company from the First Brands Group, with supply and its Ballarat factory unaffected.

stories.h: MSR sponsor's parent company enters administration
stories.t: The Australian owner of Bendix, Matt Stone Racing's naming rights sponsor since 2024, has appointed administrators. Bendix says it is business as usual and new owners will be named soon.

stories.h: Fraser returns in Mustang Cup at Sandown
stories.t: Weeks after losing his PremiAir seat, Declan Fraser will race in the Mustang Cup finale at Sandown this weekend. Lee Holdsworth also makes his debut in the series.

stories.h: McLaughlin dreams of Bathurst wildcard with van Gisbergen
stories.t: The IndyCar star says his ultimate wish is to race a Bathurst 1000 wildcard alongside his old rival Shane van Gisbergen, though NASCAR rules that out for now.

stories.h: Mostert casts himself as the underdog
stories.t: Despite winning on the Gold Coast, the reigning champion says Sandown's long straights make it a tough ask for his Toyota. His team boss expects the Supra to be strong.

stories.h: DJR calm as Kostecki heads to Sandown
stories.t: Team manager Tom Moore says DJR can recover even when off the pace. Kostecki leads the season for wins with eight but has never won in 12 starts at Sandown.

stories.h: Who plays wingman at Sandown?
stories.t: Eliminated Ryan Wood and Kai Allen can now help their teammates, while Mark Skaife says Triple Eight will eventually have to choose between Feeney and Brown.

stories.h: Brake test done, but fixes will take time
stories.t: Feeney and Brown tried several pad options in a heavily instrumented Mustang at Queensland Raceway. Supercars called it the first step in a long process, with Sandown's heavy braking zones next.

stories.h: Sinclair blames 'data engineer slop' for costly errors
stories.t: Analyst Scott Sinclair says calculation mistakes have hit results at three straight events, including the Gold Coast fuel blunders, and suggests shortcuts in AI-built team software may be to blame.

stories.h: De Pasquale could be a Sandown threat
stories.t: Team 18 was strong at Sandown last year, and Triple Eight's Mark Dutton admits he would rather have seen Wood go through, fearing the Camaro's straight-line speed there.

stories.h: Allen ready to be Payne's test car
stories.t: Eliminated Kai Allen says he will try set-ups on his car to help Matt Payne win the title, while Penrite also fights to protect its shrinking teams' championship lead.

stories.h: Prime Minister answers Mount Panorama plea
stories.t: Asked in parliament to back upgrades to the ageing track, Anthony Albanese pointed Bathurst council to a regional programme offering up to A$15 million for capital works.

stories.h: Blanchard rues 'own goal' that cost a Finals spot
stories.t: Tim Blanchard says James Golding would have made the Finals but for the double disqualification at The Bend. Speed at the Gold Coast again went unrewarded.

stories.h: 14-round 2027 calendar expected this week
stories.t: Barclay Nettlefold says all team owners now agree on changes to the Teams Racing Charter. The five holdout teams get a higher annual payment, the other seven a bonus when RACE sells.

stories.h: Lowndes warns Ford of a 'big problem' at Sandown
stories.t: With five Fords against one Chevrolet and one Toyota left, Craig Lowndes expects GM and Toyota teams to back their lone finalists, leaving Ford to work out who helps whom.

stories.h: Mostert plays down team orders flare-up
stories.t: Mostert was heard swearing on the radio when told to drop back for Ryan Wood, but says his anger was really about his own Shootout mistake. Wood now becomes his wingman at Sandown.

stories.h: Puddle cost Waters his Shootout time
stories.t: Tickford says Cam Waters' right rear left the pits above the limit but cooled to 15.741psi after hitting standing water, under the 16psi minimum. He still made Sandown comfortably.

stories.h: Grove insists Penrite has not lost speed
stories.t: Matt Payne still leads the title race despite Kai Allen's elimination, but Penrite's teams' championship lead over Red Bull Ampol has shrunk from 259 to 102 points in two rounds.

stories.h: Dane says Murray justified the switch
stories.t: Roland Dane says Cooper Murray "lifted the garage" by out-qualifying teammate Jayden Ojeda for both Gold Coast races, and expects the pair to push each other.

stories.h: Hughes skips Trans Am finale to focus on Supercars
stories.t: Erebus offered Jarrod Hughes the chance to race Trans Am and Supercars at Sandown, but the rookie will stop after this weekend's round to concentrate on his new full-time seat.

stories.h: Walkinshaw and Blanchard docked points for refuelling breaches
stories.t: Mostert keeps third, but Walkinshaw lost 30 teams' points for dropping his car with the fuel hose attached and 20 more for late fuel reports. Blanchard lost 30 for the same breach on Golding's car.

stories.h: Fuel checks clear Chevrolet of Gold Coast plot
stories.t: Supercars pumped out both late-stopping Camaros and found they could not have finished without fuel. Roland Dane called PremiAir's error a "total, utter" mess that cost Cooper Murray a top-10 finish.

stories.h: Walkinshaw and Wood question the finish
stories.t: Ryan Walkinshaw called the late Camaro stops "extremely interesting" but backed the Finals format, and said Toyota's request for Brad Jones Racing to help was refused. Wood hinted at games being played.

stories.h: Brown below the cut-line after Sunday slump
stories.t: From the front row, Will Brown faded to 11th and suspects something broke on his car. He drops to fifth and starts Sandown 12 points behind Mostert, as the first driver below the cut-line.

stories.h: Fully instrumented car for Supercars brake study
stories.t: Triple Eight's spare Mustang will carry extra infrared and pressure sensors at Queensland Raceway on Tuesday. Tim Edwards says neither teams nor Supercars fully understand the Gen3 brakes yet.

stories.h: Gold Coast crowd down six per cent
stories.t: Supercars reported 185,463 fans across the three wet days, six per cent fewer than last year despite pre-event sales tracking ahead.

stories.h: Murphy calls for Gold Coast circuit changes
stories.t: Greg Murphy says the tyre bundles brought back at the chicanes are wrecking too many cars, and wants slower corner entries instead.

stories.h: Triple Eight co-founder eyes a comeback
stories.t: Peter Butterly, one of the team's four founders in 2003, visited the Gold Coast and says a return to the pit lane is possible once he hands his European car business to his son.

stories.h: Feeney wins at home as De Pasquale scrapes into Sandown
stories.t: Broc Feeney cruised to his first Gold Coast win. Anton De Pasquale took the last Semi Final spot by 18 points, with Ryan Wood, Kai Allen and Jack Le Brocq eliminated. Matt Payne still leads.

stories.h: Toyota swap not enough to save Wood
stories.t: Walkinshaw told Chaz Mostert to drop back behind Ryan Wood, but late fuel stops for Chevrolet drivers Jarrod Hughes and Cooper Murray lifted De Pasquale past him. Erebus blamed a fuel calculation mistake.

stories.h: Mostert pit stop under investigation
stories.t: Mostert's Toyota appeared to drop to the ground before the fuel hose came off in Race 32, which the rules forbid. Shane van Gisbergen lost the 2018 Newcastle win for the same breach.

stories.h: Mostert masters the wet to book first Sandown spot
stories.t: Chaz Mostert won a soaking Race 31, his third straight Gold Coast race win, to become the first driver into the Semi Final. Pole-sitter Feeney fell to ninth after a clash with Payne.

stories.h: Reynolds ends podium drought as Team 18 weighs orders
stories.t: An early stop carried David Reynolds to second in Race 31. Team 18 had discussed asking him to let De Pasquale through, until a Payne penalty put second place within reach.

stories.h: Waters disqualified from Sunday Shootout
stories.t: Cam Waters dropped from eighth to tenth on the grid after his right rear tyre fell below the minimum pressure. Stewards accepted it was not deliberate but said the rule is mandatory.

stories.h: Feeney sweeps poles as De Pasquale qualifies 21st
stories.t: Broc Feeney led a Triple Eight front row on Sunday while Payne qualified only 12th. Kostecki was cleared of impeding Reynolds because the Camaro's headlights were off.

stories.h: Supercars books brake test before Sandown
stories.t: The category plans a brake test at Queensland Raceway on Tuesday in Triple Eight's spare car, weather permitting, after pad problems that hurt teams at Bathurst.

stories.h: Feeney takes Gold Coast pole, Mostert second
stories.t: Broc Feeney survived a lap that nearly hit every wall to beat Chaz Mostert to pole for the Finals opener. Anton De Pasquale was third, while leader Matt Payne slipped to fifth.

stories.h: Brown handed grid penalty for impeding
stories.t: Stewards dropped Will Brown two places for holding up Jack Le Brocq in qualifying. Brown said he thought the car behind was on a warm-up lap. He starts ninth.

stories.h: Kostecki misses Shootout as De Pasquale bounces back
stories.t: Bathurst winner Brodie Kostecki missed the top 10 by 0.04 seconds after kerb strikes and a last-corner error. Anton De Pasquale put his Bathurst heartbreak behind him with provisional pole.

stories.h: Three Toyotas in the top six for the first time
stories.t: Andre Heimgartner's fourth in qualifying could help Walkinshaw's Mostert and Wood by keeping their Finals rivals further back, though manufacturers cannot influence results.

stories.h: Reynolds still waiting on a 2027 deal
stories.t: David Reynolds, 41, is out of contract with Team 18 his only realistic full-time option. The team is understood to want more focus from him, and he admits he must perform better.

stories.h: Murray crashes in first PremiAir qualifying
stories.t: Cooper Murray hit the wall at the Beach Chicane and missed his final run. PremiAir's nearby workshop gives the crew time to repair the car before the race.

stories.h: Triple Eight wary of rivals' Finals tactics
stories.t: With Feeney and Brown the second and third seeds, team manager Mark Dutton says preparing for other teams' ploys has to be front of mind after losing last year's title to Mostert.

stories.h: Nicolas Hamilton rides with Waters
stories.t: The BTCC driver and brother of Lewis Hamilton called a passenger lap in Cam Waters' Tickford Mustang "insane". The extra track time raised eyebrows in other teams.

stories.h: Payne loses final practice to belt failure
stories.t: Championship leader Matt Payne managed just six laps in Gold Coast Practice 2 after a drive-belt bearing failed, while title rival Broc Feeney led a Ford top-four lockout.

stories.h: Golding fastest as wet practice catches out contenders
stories.t: James Golding topped a damp opening practice. Finals drivers Anton De Pasquale, Cam Waters and Ryan Wood all had scares, and Cooper Murray nosed into the tyres on his PremiAir debut.

stories.h: 2027 calendar announcement delayed again
stories.t: Hopes of a Friday reveal faded after the seven teams that took a cut-price deal were thought to be unhappy at a revised offer to the five holdouts. No release is expected this weekend.

stories.h: Triple Eight changes Brown's engine
stories.t: A crank angle sensor issue in Practice 1 prompted a full engine change on Will Brown's Mustang before final practice, Triple Eight's second change in as many events.

stories.h: Commins back at the track for DJR
stories.t: Brodie Kostecki's engineer George Commins is back from a fractured pelvis, working from the data room while Tom Moore stays on race engineering duties.

stories.h: Burgess: Bathurst loss felt like a death
stories.t: Team 18 boss Adrian Burgess compared the last-lap fuel defeat to losing Ayrton Senna, and blamed the wrong cell being picked on the team's fuel sheet.

stories.h: GM plays down Finals team games
stories.t: With six Fords facing two Chevrolets and two Toyotas, GM's Simon McNamara says Chevrolet's only aim is getting De Pasquale and Le Brocq through. Rules bar manufacturers from giving team orders.

stories.h: Why Dane chose Murray
stories.t: Roland Dane says Cooper Murray is fast and hungry, and signed him to 2028 hoping PremiAir will have two drivers capable of running in the top 10 next year.

stories.h: Ingall pushing for another Herne Bathurst drive
stories.t: After finishing 19th on his Bathurst debut with Garry Rogers Motorsport, Nathan Herne says Russell Ingall is working behind the scenes to land him another start.

stories.h: Sandown 500 tipped to return in 2027
stories.t: A two-driver Sandown 500 could return in an expanded Enduro Cup if the 2027 calendar runs to 14 rounds, but five teams remain locked in a funding standoff with Supercars owner RACE.

stories.h: Brown flying since 'restrictor gate' fix
stories.t: Will Brown was 245 points back in March. Since a faulty restrictor was fixed he has outscored everyone, and he plans to stay aggressive despite heavy rain forecast all weekend.

stories.h: Holdsworth vows to return to Bathurst
stories.t: Lee Holdsworth says his fuel-hit 23rd Bathurst "keeps hitting me every day", but he expects to be back with Team 18 for the 2027 enduros.

stories.h: Whincup calls Supercars' business model 'poor'
stories.t: Jamie Whincup says teams see no media-rights or gate money, unlike AFL and NRL clubs whose leagues cover around 60 per cent of their costs.

stories.h: Wood ready to go for broke
stories.t: Ninth in points and 18 short of the cut-line, Ryan Wood will chase a race win at the Gold Coast, which would send him straight through to the next Finals round.

stories.h: Blanchard team turns Cameron's Mustang pink
stories.t: Aaron Cameron's car carries a breast cancer tribute to a team mechanic's late mother-in-law, while Cody Golding's sister car runs new Dayco colours.

stories.h: Triple Eight moves into defence work
stories.t: Triple Eight Engineering has earned aerospace-grade certification and is stepping up work on defence land vehicles, alongside the parts it already makes for Qantas.

stories.h: Perkins keeps an open mind after Bathurst pain
stories.t: Jack Perkins' Bathurst ended with power steering failure on the formation lap. He would like to return in 2027 but is open-minded about what comes next.

stories.h: Crompton tells his side of the TV axing
stories.t: Neil Crompton says he was offered only Tailem Bend and Bathurst on terms worth about 80 per cent less, and denies issuing an all-or-nothing ultimatum before leaving the broadcast.

stories.h: Payne wants to stay top seed through the rain
stories.t: The championship leader starts the Gold Coast 111 points clear of the cut-line but has never stood on the podium there, and expects a testing wet weekend on public roads.

stories.h: Why rain could shake up the Gold Coast
stories.t: Race engineer Scott Sinclair notes the last wet Gold Coast race had nearly four times as many passes as the dry day before, at a track where overtaking is normally the hardest of the year.

stories.h: Le Brocq the Finals' ultimate underdog
stories.t: Saturday's race will be his 100th since his last podium, the 2023 Darwin win. Matt Stone says MSR must step up to give him a real title shot.

stories.h: Gray expects a big step in his second year
stories.t: DJR's rookie Rylan Gray credits extra driver training and leaving the set-up to Kostecki for his recent gains, and says he will help his team-mate's title push however he can.

stories.h: Gold Coast run club event cancelled
stories.t: Supercars has scrapped Friday's Track Club run with Nedd Brockmann, citing demand and timing. Ticket holders will be contacted directly.

stories.h: Red Bull Ampol goes 'Summer Edition' for the Gold Coast
stories.t: Feeney and Brown unveiled a bright one-off livery in Surfers Paradise, the team's second Gold Coast special in two years.

stories.h: Blanchard moves on from The Bend disqualification
stories.t: The driver-time breach cost Golding 182 points and his Finals place. Tim Blanchard says the team has moved on, with Lochie Dalton 114 points clear in Super2.

stories.h: No NASCAR wildcards at the Adelaide Grand Final
stories.t: Chevrolet's plan for Connor Zilisch and a Toyota bid linked to Ty Gibbs have both been shelved, V8 Sleuth understands, so no Cup Series driver will join the field in November.

stories.h: Gold Coast forecast turns wetter
stories.t: Up to 40mm is now forecast for Friday. Thomas Randle says the first dry laps could come in Saturday's Shootout or even the race, and Broc Feeney fears sessions being lost.

stories.h: Erebus boss sees a future star in Hughes
stories.t: Barry Ryan says Jarrod Hughes, who debuts solo this weekend, has the appeal of a Lowndes or Mostert, pointing to his cool head leading in heavy rain at The Bend.

stories.h: Feeney split on the new Beach Chicane bundles
stories.t: Feeney is happy with the bundle on the right but not those on the left, which could catch a driver who gets the entry wrong. He was caught in the 2022 pile-up there.

stories.h: Mostert back in the chassis he gave up last year
stories.t: The spare Mostert races this weekend is WR 029, the car he left mid-2025 before his title run. He blames the set-up direction at the time, not the car.

stories.h: Feeney still chasing a home win
stories.t: The Gold Coast local has four straight podiums at Surfers Paradise but no win, and last year's defeat to Mostert on fuel economy still stings.

stories.h: Kostecki wary of another Gold Coast mistake
stories.t: His Turn 1 qualifying crash here last year ended his title hopes. Now arguably the favourite, he says one error in the wet could cost the whole weekend.

stories.h: Straight-line work behind MSR's Bathurst speed
stories.t: Head of engineering Jack Bellotti says years of focusing on straight-line speed finally paid off, ending a 17-month podium drought.

stories.h: Heimgartner the Finals nearly man again
stories.t: Seventh at Bathurst with Bryce Fullwood was the best Toyota finish and, he says, BJR's best-run race in years, but it left him 11th, just outside the Finals.

stories.h: Moore stays on Kostecki's radio for the Gold Coast
stories.t: DJR is keeping its Bathurst-winning set-up, with Tom Moore engineering the #17. George Commins may return trackside in a support role as he recovers from his mountain bike crash.

stories.h: Rain forecast for the Finals opener
stories.t: Up to 30mm is forecast for Friday's practice and qualifying at Surfers Paradise. The last wet Gold Coast race, in 2018, was abandoned.

stories.h: De Pasquale: Bathurst will hurt for a long time
stories.t: The Team 18 driver admits morale is low but says the Finals are a separate fight. He starts the Gold Coast seventh, just nine points above the cut for Sandown.

stories.h: Walkinshaw's Carl Faux heads to NASCAR
stories.t: The Briton who led Walkinshaw's technical revival has finished up after Bathurst and joins Jimmie Johnson's Legacy Motor Club, which expands to three Toyotas in the Cup Series next year.

stories.h: Late nights get Walkinshaw's Supras ready
stories.t: Chaz Mostert says the crew worked until 10 or 11pm all week to fix Wood's car and build his spare. The champion starts eighth, nine points behind De Pasquale.

stories.h: Gold Coast qualifying moves to Friday
stories.t: Saturday's grid will be set by a 30-minute session on Friday afternoon, so every day of the Finals opener carries something at stake.

stories.h: Gold Coast moved off Seven's main channel
stories.t: With horse racing, rugby league and AFLW also on, Saturday's race airs on 7two and Sunday's on 7mate in Australia.

stories.h: MSR not in the Finals just to make up numbers
stories.t: Jack Le Brocq is the team's first Finals entrant, and Matt Stone wants to carry the momentum from MSR's double top-four Bathurst into the Gold Coast.

stories.h: Grove goes pink for breast cancer charity
stories.t: Grove's Mustangs and drivers' kit get pink touches for the Gold Coast, with the gloves to be auctioned as part of a $350,000 drive for the McGrath Foundation.

stories.h: Courtney on the moment Team 18's win slipped away
stories.t: Sitting beside Lee Holdsworth in the garage, James Courtney had already told him he'd be a two-time winner. Neither knew about the fuel problem until the car stopped.

stories.h: Why six drivers just missed the Finals
stories.t: Supercars.com looks at how Heimgartner, Randle, Golding, Ojeda and Reynolds fell short as Jack Le Brocq took the last place. Golding's slip from a 107-point buffer after The Bend hurt most.

stories.h: Davison tops the Bathurst co-driver rankings
stories.t: On lap time analysis, Will Davison was the quickest co-driver, ahead of Todd Hazelwood, Aaron Seton and Lee Holdsworth. Seton set the fastest co-driver lap of the race.

stories.h: Phillip Island's championship winners
stories.t: With the Island back from 2027, V8 Sleuth lists every winner of its 62 championship races since 1976, a list once dominated by Glenn Seton.

stories.h: Bathurst reshuffles the Gold Coast pit lane
stories.t: Walkinshaw's 44-point Bathurst lets Tickford take third in the teams' standings and the better garages, while MSR moves Jack Le Brocq up to the middle of pit lane. Triple Eight cut Penrite's lead to 190.

stories.h: Triple Eight plays the long game in the Finals
stories.t: Team manager Mark Dutton says the plan is consistency rather than all-or-nothing, with Feeney and Brown starting the Gold Coast second and third and a buffer to the cut-line.

stories.h: Brown surprised by his quick warning flag
stories.t: Will Brown says he was defending for a podium, not the win, when Kostecki caught him late on, and was taken aback by how fast race control showed him the bad sportsmanship flag.

stories.h: New commentary team earns its stripes
stories.t: Speedcafe reckons Richard Craill, Garth Tander and Greg Murphy delivered when it mattered most at Bathurst, after a rocky start to the year without Neil Crompton and Mark Skaife.

stories.h: Pye's unwanted Bathurst record
stories.t: Second with Will Brown was Scott Pye's third Bathurst runner-up finish, equalling the record for a driver yet to win it. He says it has made him hungrier still.

stories.h: Seven things Bathurst taught us
stories.t: V8 Sleuth's verdict covers the late parity fix, Kostecki's relentless drive back to the front and the new commentary team rising to the occasion.

stories.h: Murray's rare two-team season, again
stories.t: Only three drivers in 20 years have raced for two teams in one season, and Cooper Murray is already one of them after 2024. He does it again at PremiAir.

stories.h: Murray meets his new PremiAir crew
stories.t: Days after sixth at Bathurst, Cooper Murray had his seat fitting on the Gold Coast. Simon Hodge will engineer him, and sim work with Jayden Ojeda comes before only two practice sessions.

stories.h: Davison's Bathurst pace beat Le Brocq's
stories.t: Lap data shared on The Undercut ranked Will Davison 14th for pace, ahead of fourth-placed Jack Le Brocq, suggesting he and Payne could have been on the podium without their penalties.

stories.h: Phillip Island returns as a Finals round from 2027
stories.t: Supercars goes back to the Island for the first time since 2019 on a five-year deal, with the new Phillip Island 500 forming part of the Finals series from 2027 to 2031.

stories.h: Older brake pad compound back for the Gold Coast
stories.t: After three rounds of complaints about pads wearing and fading, Brad Jones says the category will revert to a previously used compound for the Finals opener.

stories.h: Tyre bundles return to the Beach Chicane
stories.t: To meet the circuit's safety licence, bundles go back at Turns 8 and 9, but set a car's width from the kerb so drivers can still attack it. Last year's flying cars reportedly worried the FIA.

stories.h: The sum behind Team 18's empty tank
stories.t: Speedcafe understands the #18's last-stint calculator assumed the car had been filled at its penultimate stop. It had been short-filled on lap 123, leaving it about three seconds of fuel short.

stories.h: Harri Jones makes his case for a 2027 seat
stories.t: A late call-up as Jack Le Brocq's co-driver brought fourth at Bathurst and a Finals spot for MSR. Jones is thought to be under consideration at Team 18.

stories.h: Hughes ready for a Surfers Paradise baptism
stories.t: Jarrod Hughes has never raced on the Gold Coast but says he loves street circuits. His three-round stint is expected to lead to a full-time Erebus seat in 2027, though nothing is confirmed.

stories.h: DJR hopes to have Commins back for the Gold Coast
stories.t: Kostecki's race engineer missed Bathurst after a mountain bike crash, with team manager Tom Moore stepping in. DJR says he will return when he is ready.

stories.h: Ford camp says parity didn't decide Bathurst
stories.t: Jamie Whincup believes both makes had an equal shot, and Cam Waters won't blame the Camaro's straight-line speed for Tickford's off weekend, expecting the Mustang to suit the Finals tracks better.

stories.h: Red Bull Ampol promo Mustang ends up in a ditch
stories.t: A road car in the team's colours left the M1 near Yatala. The team confirmed nobody was hurt but said nothing more.

stories.h: Cameron stays at Blanchard on a multi-year deal
stories.t: Aaron Cameron has been rewarded for a breakthrough year, including a first podium in Sydney, with a new multi-year contract. It completes Blanchard Racing's 2027 line-up alongside James Golding.

stories.h: Murray brings his family #36 to PremiAir
stories.t: Cooper Murray will race the #36 from the Gold Coast onwards, the number his father used and he carried through karts and Carrera Cup. It last ran full-time in Supercars in 2014.

stories.h: Where the 2027 grid stands after the GM shuffle
stories.t: Seventeen drivers are now signed for 2027 and six teams have full line-ups. Open seats remain at DJR, Brad Jones Racing, Team 18 and Matt Stone Racing, with David Reynolds' future unclear.

stories.h: Walkinshaw counts the cost of Bathurst
stories.t: Mostert's 25G hit damaged his Supra's chassis badly enough to need around 40 hours of fabrication, hence the spare. Ryan Wood's car, hit twice over the weekend, is being repaired for the Gold Coast.

stories.h: Skaife: Team 18's fuel error was unforgivable
stories.t: Six-time Bathurst winner Mark Skaife says Team 18 should have checked the final fill by hand rather than trusting its software, while feeling for De Pasquale and Holdsworth.

stories.h: Randle's Finals miss stings Tickford
stories.t: For the first time, Tickford starts the Finals with a car out of contention. The team says Thomas Randle will still chase wins on the Gold Coast, where both drivers have strong records.

stories.h: Seton in no hurry after his Bathurst podium
stories.t: Third with Zach Bates made Aaron Seton the third generation of his family on the Bathurst podium. Asked about a full-time return, he said his focus has been on being a dependable co-driver.

stories.h: How Bates announced himself at Bathurst
stories.t: V8 Sleuth looks back at Zach Bates' weekend: 18th in points beforehand, then the two fastest Gen3 laps of Mount Panorama, Shootout pole and a podium.

stories.h: DJR keeps its Bathurst-winning Mustang
stories.t: Dick Johnson Racing owns none of its earlier Bathurst winners, so this one isn't for sale. Kostecki races it again on the Gold Coast, and the finishing panels have been kept aside.

stories.h: Triple Eight and Grove raise $200,000 for charity
stories.t: A side bet on which team beat the other across the Bathurst weekend, topped up by both owners, has raised $200,000 for domestic violence charity RizeUp.

stories.h: Murray signs with PremiAir to the end of 2028
stories.t: Cooper Murray's move from Erebus is a long one: the #777 Camaro for the last three rounds of 2026, then two full seasons alongside Jayden Ojeda. He joins the team on the Gold Coast this week.

links.label: V8 Sleuth: Murray on his first week

stories.h: Fraser says the PremiAir exit wasn't his call
stories.t: Dropped after one season, Declan Fraser says he is deeply disappointed by how it unfolded but has no plans to give up on a Supercars future.

stories.h: Supercars driver tipped for a NASCAR Cup outing
stories.t: Word in the NASCAR paddock is that an Australian Supercars driver is in line for RFK Racing's #6 car in 2027, most likely for two road-course races. Cam Waters and Broc Feeney are the obvious names.

stories.h: Tickford left hunting for Bathurst speed
stories.t: A mistake-free race brought only ninth and 15th. Rod Nash admits the Mustangs simply lacked pace, and Cam Waters heads to the Gold Coast as sixth seed.

stories.h: Where Team 18's fuel sums went wrong
stories.t: Race engineer Scott Sinclair's analysis picks out the #18's fifth stop, short-filled by about 12 litres, as a likely turning point, and shows how close DJR's slow brake change came to costing them too.

stories.h: Kostecki nearly crashed after taking the lead
stories.t: Overcome with emotion after passing the stranded #18, Kostecki almost went off at The Cutting on the final lap, he told his podcast. He hadn't even been sure it was the last lap.

stories.h: Johnson feels for old rival Schwerkolt
stories.t: Despite their bitter 2010 split, Dick Johnson says losing Bathurst the way Team 18 did is never nice, and ranks DJR's fifth win alongside his famous 1981 victory.

stories.h: Brothers on opposite sides of the finish
stories.t: Team 18 manager Mitch Croke and his brother Shane, part of DJR's pit crew, shared a tearful hug in pit lane as one garage celebrated and the other was left heartbroken.

stories.h: BRT looks to the Gold Coast after Finals miss
stories.t: Eighth at Bathurst wasn't enough to get James Golding into the Finals, but Blanchard Racing brought both cars home undamaged and heads north with confidence.

stories.h: MSR engineer pays up on his Bathurst bet
stories.t: Data engineer Blake Holden promised to shave his head if Matt Stone Racing took pole or a podium. Zach Bates delivered both, and the team held him to it.

stories.h: GM shuffles three drivers before the Finals
stories.t: PremiAir has dropped Declan Fraser for the last three rounds. Cooper Murray moves across from Erebus, and 21-year-old Jarrod Hughes takes Murray's #99 Camaro for his solo debut at the Gold Coast.

stories.h: Software, not a person, ran De Pasquale dry
stories.t: Team 18 says a fault in its fuel strategy software under-filled the #18 Camaro at the final stop. Nobody loses their job, and De Pasquale starts the Finals as seventh seed.

stories.h: Mostert gets a spare Supra for the Gold Coast
stories.t: The champion's Bathurst car goes on the jig after his lap 156 hit at Forrest's Elbow. He races chassis WR 029, a former Ford converted to Toyota spec.

stories.h: Brown and Pye bank the Enduro Cup
stories.t: Second at Bathurst after fourth at The Bend sealed the Enduro Cup, and the bonus points lift Will Brown to third seed for the Finals opener.

stories.h: Grove regroups after Payne's penalty-hit Bathurst
stories.t: Two penalties left Payne fifth and the sister car limped home with brake failure. Payne still starts the Finals as top seed.

stories.h: Dick Johnson in tears as the #17 steals it
stories.t: The 81-year-old's reaction summed up DJR's last-lap win, and the team's CEO admits they were as stunned as anyone.

stories.h: Lowndes: you can't script Bathurst
stories.t: The seven-time winner's column on why the Great Race is so easy to lose, and the fire it leaves in drivers like Zach Bates.

stories.h: Making sense of 5:26pm
stories.t: An opinion piece on the human errors on both sides, DJR's slow stop and Team 18's fuel call, that shaped the finish.

stories.h: Feeney admits the #88 was just slow
stories.t: Eleventh at Bathurst, and Feeney won't pin it all on the brakes while his team-mate Brown finished second.

stories.h: Bates proud of his first podium
stories.t: The MSR rookie and Aaron Seton took third after a weekend that also brought a qualifying record and Shootout pole.
